# @motifx-community/ui

> UI components for MotifJS (@motifx/core) on the MotifJS design system. Version 0.1.0-beta.10: a preview, its API may still change before 1.0.

Built on MotifJS (`@motifx/core`): a component is an object, made in JSX or with `new`, whose every prop takes a value or a function (`Bind<T>`); `x-model` binds a value two-way. The look is the design system’s (`@motifx-community/design-system`): five design languages (`data-design-language`), light and dark themes, density.

## Start

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, set up Vite, styles, design languages, the kit’s languages

## Get started

- [@motifx-community/ui](docs/home.md): Components for MotifJS: objects you create when you need them, show anywhere and dispose when you are done, drawn from the MotifJS design system's tokens.
- [Showcase: an order screen](docs/showcase.md): An order entry screen built with the kit, structured the way a MotifJS application is normally built: state and operations live in a model (`OrderModel`),…
- [Showcase: a smart home](docs/showcase-home.md): A smart home panel for a tablet, built with the kit as a MotifJS application of its own: a rail of screens, the day and the home's state at the top, and…
- [Design tokens](docs/tokens.md): The token system has five layers. The first four (primitives, design language scales, semantic tokens per theme, and density) come from…

- [Keyboard and focus](docs/keyboard.md): Every control follows the same rules for Tab order, the active control of a container, focus handling, `&File` access keys and application-wide shortcuts.
- [Commands and shortcuts](docs/commands.md): A command of the app is defined once: its text, icon, keys, state and action. Menus, toolbars and ribbons name it, its keys run it, and the user can give it…
- [Language](docs/language.md): `uiLocale` controls the strings that controls display, the locale used for dates and numbers, and the text direction. The kit has one `uiLocale`, and each…

## Charts

- [Chart](docs/chart.md): Displays lines, areas, bars, scatter points and bubbles on a shared value axis. The chart has no dependencies, takes its appearance from the design…
- [Chart: Lines and areas](docs/chart-lines.md): Lines and areas show how values change along an axis: over time, or from one category to the next.
- [Chart: Bars](docs/chart-bars.md): Bars compare amounts. They stand on a common baseline, so lengths compare exactly, side by side, stacked, or on their side for long names.
- [Chart: Scatter and bubble](docs/chart-scatter.md): Scatter and bubble charts place each row by two numbers, to show how they relate.
- [Chart: Pie and donut](docs/chart-pie.md): A pie or a donut splits one whole into its parts, for a share seen at a glance.
- [Chart: Funnel](docs/chart-funnel.md): A funnel follows a quantity through stages in order, and shows how much of it is left at each one.
- [Chart: Radar](docs/chart-radar.md): A radar compares several measures at once, for one or more items.
- [Chart: Heat map](docs/chart-heatmap.md): A heat map shows a value for each pair of two categories as a color.
- [Chart: Ranges](docs/chart-ranges.md): Ranges show a low and a high value for each position, as a band or as floating bars.
- [Chart: Candles](docs/chart-candles.md): Candles show the first, highest, lowest and last price for each position.
- [Chart: Waterfall](docs/chart-waterfall.md): A waterfall shows how a starting value becomes an end value through changes up and down.
- [Chart: Zoom and large data](docs/chart-zoom.md): Large data stays quick: long lines are thinned to the width with their peaks kept, and the reader zooms in for detail.
- [Chart: Live data](docs/chart-live.md): A chart follows its data: reactive values redraw it, and live data moves along with the latest values.
- [Chart: References and selection](docs/chart-references.md): Reference lines and bands give the values a target, a limit or a period, and the reader can choose values to act on.
- [Sparkline](docs/sparkline.md): A chart the size of a word, for a trend beside a number, in a sentence or in a row of a table. It draws a line, an area, bars, or wins and losses, and marks…

## Gauges

- [Gauge](docs/gauge.md): Shows a value against its scale, as an arc, a circle or a straight bar. Ranges give stretches of the scale a meaning, markers and marks point at values, and…
- [Gauge: Circular](docs/gauge-circular.md): A circular gauge shows its value on an arc or a whole circle, with the value written in the middle. It reads best for one value whose scale the reader…
- [Gauge: Linear](docs/gauge-linear.md): A linear gauge shows its value on a straight bar, across or upright. Bars fit in narrow places, line up in lists, and compare well side by side.
- [Gauge: Scales](docs/gauge-scales.md): The scale tells the reader how to read the value: its ends, ticks with their values, or nothing at all.
- [Gauge: Ranges](docs/gauge-ranges.md): Ranges give stretches of the scale a meaning, such as normal, high and critical. They show as a band beside the track, and the fill takes the color of the…
- [Gauge: Markers](docs/gauge-markers.md): A marker points at the value: a needle from the middle of an arc, a shape on or beside the track, or a callout that writes the value.
- [Gauge: Marks](docs/gauge-marks.md): Marks show other values on the scale besides the gauge's own, such as a target, a limit, or the lowest and highest expected.
- [Gauge: Base value](docs/gauge-base.md): The fill starts at the start of the scale, or at a base value inside it. A scale with values on both sides of a target then fills from the target, either way.
- [Gauge: Dashboards](docs/gauge-dashboards.md): Gauges of different kinds put together, all following the same values. Each gauge keeps its own scale, so readers compare values by their meaning, not by…
- [BarGauge](docs/bar-gauge.md): Shows several values side by side as bars bent round one middle, each against the same scale. It compares a few values at a glance, in little room.
- [BarGauge: Labels and legend](docs/bar-gauge-labels.md): Each value can be written at the end of its bar, named in a legend, and shown with its name under the pointer.
- [BarGauge: Data](docs/bar-gauge-data.md): A bar gauge reads numbers, or rows through their fields, and follows them as they change.
- [BarGauge: Angles and size](docs/bar-gauge-angles.md): How far the bars go round and which way they face fit a bar gauge to the room it has.

- [DataGrid: Scrolling](docs/datagrid-scrolling.md): The `mode` prop determines how rows are reached. Every mode renders only the visible rows from a small pool, so the page never holds one element per row.

- [DataGrid: API reference](docs/datagrid-api.md): Up to 0.1.0-beta.8, the root of the content that `cell`, `groupCell`, `headerCell`, a band's `headerCell` and the detail `template` return must not carry…
